report.summary: I reviewed only the supplied packet: lib/source-business-evidence.ts, lib/delivery-assessment.ts, lib/business-checks.ts, the cycle-13 countercheck record, the plan record and the skill file. I found no genuinely reachable current source defect in the narrow deterministic/evidence relation dimension. All 20 countercases in the packet support the actual guards: element children in p/li are rejected at line 102; raw markup in td is rejected at line 44 and non-text AST children at line 47; the anchored amount() regex at lines 126-129 rejects compound tails; parse5 always materialises a body, so the implicit-body cases pass. In addition, selectors at line 34/97 reject hidden, inert, aria-hidden, style and span attrs; leaf and body counts keep uniqueness; multi-checks are all-witnessed before a covered result. I make no approval or sign-off claim. The 20 cases are Codex-authored scripted checks whose expected 'want' values are the author's expectations, not an independent test of the guards. The prior invalid-JSON reviewer reply is not treated as agreement, and this reply makes no approval commitment. Actual model behaviour after these guards is not established: the new prompt/response cycle and known-item reruns remain unexecuted, and no runtime, browser or provider check was performed.
limitations: Read-only static review of the supplied fragments only. No files were changed, no shell/test/parse5/model execution was performed, and no runtime check, test result or live-provider behaviour is claimed.

Not established by supplied source: the internals of hasUncertainSourceBodyCopyAtFile (lib/exact-copy-evidence.ts), getBusinessCheckPlan input validation chain beyond business-checks.ts, and other callers of these exports.

The 20 countercases are Codex-authored production-entry-point scripts whose 'want' values are author expectations; their pass does not independently prove guard semantics, and the record itself labels the scope non-exhaustive.

Model behaviour after these guards is unverified. The new first live cycle and the known-item reruns are not executed in this review, so prompt/filter effectiveness for the cited-wrong-page (about.html) case and for known regressions remains uncertain.

No conclusion is drawn about opponent source tests, award scoring, overall winner quality or relative award quality. The award record is used only as the planned narrow deterministic/evidence relation dimension.

The record retains reviewValid:false / reviewErrors['report_not_json'] and reviewAccepted:false. This reply does not approve, accept or sign off that artifact; it only adds an independent review result.

Deliberately narrow supported formats (text-only p/li, two-cell text-only rows, literal AUD/USD ISO amounts) produce conservative 'unknown' for split or complex layouts. This is a documented limit, not a defect finding here.
Non-UTF-8/binary encoding, CSS-rendered content and raster pixels are not evaluated.
